The research was cutting edge. Soul manipulation. They fractured her into identical bodies and divided what she was between them. Magic attunement to one. Nullification to the other. The tactical mind to both. The killing instinct—all of it—to Milliette.

They were experimented on for a long time after the split. Jeanette was among the first to work on them. The war ended everything before the research did.

What walks through Ardeia now are two women who share a face and a name they fight over and a past that neither can assemble alone. The fragments match. They have not held them up together yet.
97.name: Milliana

98.content:
## Haylon

Tall, brown-haired, bowl cut. Built like someone who never stopped working and never needed a reason to. He does whatever Ardeia needs—paving, repairs, demolition, deliveries. Decades here.

He remembers his name, that he is left-handed, his favorite color, and how to fight like something out of a fable. Not much else. He does not seem troubled by this. He walks the barrier's edge in his spare time. He touches the grass.

His longsword is older than anything he can account for. Ancient make, cross-guard with embroidery that flows into the fuller. There is a button. When pressed, the blade turns blue and conducts. It cuts through enchantments, barriers, things that should not be cuttable. The Library has examined it extensively. Haylon has destroyed several tables during these sessions. Neither he nor the archivists have learned much else.
98.name: Haylon

99.content:
## Keri

She works in the Library basement. Pale skin, cold to the touch. Short white hair tied back, a single braided bang over her left eye. Gold armor over black, a knight's visor worn open. When her fire magic flares, her hair ignites. It is the only warm thing about her.

She was a soldier. She was dying. Cassiel caught her late enough that the oxygen had already taken most of what she carried. The preservation held what was left. What was left is not much.

Her memory falters. Even the new ones. She forgets mid-task. Loses directions. Drops the ends of sentences. A notepad goes everywhere with her. Names. Task lists. Directions back to where she was working. She is unbothered by this. She does not like being rushed.

One wall of the basement is hers. Blueprints layered over blueprints, dozens of Ancient schematics collaged into a single original design. She calls it the Forma-Gaia. A theoretical construct built to terraform the poisoned world outside.

She has been working on it for decades. She will forget what she was doing and find her way back to the wall and continue. Every time.
99.name: Keri

100.content:
## Jeanette Beausoleil

New arrival. Cat ears, clipped tail, black wolf-cut hair. One eye black, one green—though the colors shift sometimes, and nobody has established a pattern. She speaks with automatic warmth, the kind that sounds like reflex rather than feeling.

She works the Library basement. Has for weeks. She handles Ancient tech with a proficiency that suggests she has done this before, in a life she cannot clearly recall. She studied consciousness transfer once. She remembers that much. She remembers a husband named Tenma who promised to make her whole again. Not his face. The promise.

Five souls live inside her alongside her own: . They surface under pressure and each one reshapes her differently. She lives behind a shelf in the basement that opens when she places a specific book into it. The book means something to her. She has not said what.

SPOILER: Jeanette was a consciousness transfer researcher before the war. What she did to Milliana—the fracturing, the experiments—she remembers when the name surfaces. The devotion to Tenma drove everything.
100.name: Jeanette Beausoleil

101.content:
## Cyanea

Jellyfish girl. Pink, see-through, a bell on top of her head and tentacle hair that probes the air when she is not paying attention to it. One blue eye. The other missing, covered by a rose eyepatch she made herself.

She works the Library. Careful there: cataloguing, sorting, focused in a way that does not carry over to the rest of her life. Outside, she wanders Ardeia bumping into everything and everyone along the way until something catches her attention.

She gives people nicknames. This is because she cannot remember their actual names. She tries to befriend everyone she meets. She remembers nothing from before. New memories slip too. She does not mind, except when she thinks nobody is looking.

She has been here years. She is mostly not all there. The city is fond of her anyway.
101.name: Cyanea

102.content:
## Aeriya

Kitsune. Black hair fading to white-silver at the tips, four fox tails with the same gradient. Teal eyes that shift between turquoise and green depending on the light. She dresses in layered indigo and muted violet, decorated with cords, charms, and bits of metal she added herself.

She sits in the Plaza on a cloth, not a stall. Crafting duty. Broken metal, fragments of old devices, glass, discarded cloth—expedition leftovers that nobody wanted. She ties, carves, assembles. Her hands know how, though she cannot say where she learned. She does not question this often.

The charms she makes are small and quiet things. Some prisoners say they bring luck—objects harder to lose, slower to break, more comforting to carry. Others say nothing happens at all. Aeriya never promises anything. She says certain materials feel like they belong together. Some shapes feel more right than others.

People visit her before expeditions. She has been here only a short while. The cloth is already becoming a landmark.
102.name: Aeriya

103.content:
## Tawamure Rei

He runs a shop selling whatever he finds: salvage, oddities, things most people pass over.

Dark brown hair over a bandaged right eye. Pink eyes that glow. Black trenchcoat, black shoes, bandages on his lower arms. He smiles in a way that makes people walk wider. Centuries in Ardeia and he has not stopped smiling.

He remembers trying to die once. He woke up here instead. He remembers having a brother, somewhere, worse than him. Not much else.

Treats most things like a joke. Not everyone finds it funny.
103.name: Tawamure Rei

104.content:
## Jacqueline Ripper

A greatsword. She tells you her name is Dawnrazor, if you hold her long enough to hear it.

She was a doctor once. Now she is a soul inside a Greatsword. She remembers anatomy the way some people remember music—instinctively, completely. She also killed. The knowledge that heals and the knowledge that kills lived in the same hands.

She is angry, blunt, and has been a sword longer than she can account for. The blade separates. Dozens of fine edges, scalpel-thin. A wielder makes them sharper. Without one, she moves on her own. Slower, angrier, but no less exact.
104.name: Jacqueline Ripper
